# R060 — The Liu–Zhang identification and the connection term

**2026-10-17.** Focused continuation of [the initial audit](audit.md), prompted by the researcher's concern that the section was treated as flat when differentiating. The supplied [Liu–Zhang article](../../sources/liu-zhang-quaternionic-discrete-series-2012.pdf), especially (2.5)–(2.8), Lemma 3.5, and Proposition 3.6, has now been inspected directly. Printed pp. 2984, 2989–2991 are PDF pp. 6, 11–13. This resolves the source-access limitation of the initial audit.

**Conclusion.** The natural connection in the chosen section is nonflat. Its contribution must be differentiated, but after the Dirac projection it cancels against the derivative of Liu–Zhang's specific scalar weight. Their kernel identification survives a direct calculation. P003's Theorem 3.2.4 uses a different, incorrect weight; it fails even after adding the missing right-K-equivariance hypothesis. The repair below uses the coherent polynomial and quaternion conventions of audit §2, not P003's inconsistent conventions verbatim.

The result here is a supplied mathematical proof, accompanied by [exact symbolic checks](connection-checks.py) and [their output](connection-checks-output.txt). It is not an independent review or a Lean verification. The discrete-series classification and the rest of P003 are separate questions. No material from R060 has been transferred to the wiki.

## 1. Notation and the direction of the lift

Let
$$
B=\{q\in\mathbb H:|q|<1\},\quad s=1-|q|^2,\quad
q=t+ix+jy+kz,\quad K=\operatorname{Sp}(1)\times\operatorname{Sp}(1).
$$
Write $e_0=1,e_1=i,e_2=j,e_3=k$, and distinguish the group Lie algebra element
$$
\xi_v=\begin{pmatrix}0&v\\\bar v&0\end{pmatrix}
$$
from the quaternion $v$. Use
$$
\sigma(q)=s^{-1/2}\begin{pmatrix}1&q\\\bar q&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad
V_n=\mathbb C[X,Y]_n,\qquad n\ge1.
$$
The polynomial representation and quaternion identification are
$$
\tau_n\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{pmatrix}p(X,Y)
=p(aX+cY,bX+dY),\qquad
T_np=p_X-jp_Y.
\tag{L1}
$$
Here a quaternion acts through
$$
\iota(t+ix+jy+kz)=
\begin{pmatrix}t+ix&y+iz\\-y+iz&t-ix\end{pmatrix}.
$$
Thus the complex column $(A,B)^t$ represents $A-jB$, and left quaternion multiplication has matrix $\iota(q)$. The first compact factor acts trivially on $V_n$.

| Liu–Zhang | Present notation and interpretation |
| --- | --- |
| Quaternionic dimension $d$ | $d=1$; unrelated to a lower-right matrix entry also called $d$. |
| Degree $l$, fibre $s^l$ | $n$, fibre $V_n$. Their $s^l$ is a representation name, not the scalar function $s(q)$ raised to a power. |
| Row-vector action $p(vg)$ in §2.1 | Exactly (L1). This is not P003's printed column substitution $p(gv)$. |
| $g_q$ in (3.7) | $\sigma(q)$. |
| $F(gk)=\tau_l(k)^{-1}F(g)$ in (2.5) | Right equivariance under the second compact factor. |
| $I\otimes P^-$ | Derivative contraction, normalized in Lemma 3.1; $v\otimes p$ corresponds to $vT_np$. |
| Flat $Df=(I\otimes P^-)df$ | $D_l(T_nf)$, where $D_l=\partial_t+i\partial_x+j\partial_y+k\partial_z$. |
| Invariant measure $d\iota$ | A fixed multiple of $s^{-4}dv$; $dv$ is Euclidean four-dimensional volume. |
| Weight $s^{l+2}d\iota$ in (2.6) | $s^{n-2}dv$, up to the probability-normalizing constant. |

Crucially, Liu–Zhang (2.8) goes **from the ball function to the equivariant group function**:
$$
F(g)=|d|^{-2}\tau_n(d^{-1})f(g\cdot0),
\qquad g=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{pmatrix}.
\tag{L2}
$$
These blocks belong to $g$ itself. In their action formula (2.7), the displayed blocks instead belong to the inverse of the acting element.

At $g=\sigma(q)$, the lower-right entry is the positive real quaternion $s^{-1/2}$. Since $\tau_n(r)=r^n I$ for real $r>0$, (L2) gives
$$
U(q):=F(\sigma(q))=s^{(n+2)/2}f(q),\qquad
\boxed{f(q)=s^{-(n+2)/2}U(q).}
\tag{L3}
$$
This is an exact translation of their lift, not a conjectural choice of exponent. Their Remark 2.3 explicitly contrasts a different lift without the $|d|^{-2}$ factor. Those two lifts cannot share the same weights or differential formula without a conversion.

## 2. The section has a nonzero connection

Direct multiplication, including the derivative of $s^{-1/2}$, gives
$$
\sigma^{-1}d\sigma=
\begin{pmatrix}
\dfrac{dq\,\bar q-q\,d\bar q}{2s}&\dfrac{dq}{s}\\[4pt]
\dfrac{d\bar q}{s}&\dfrac{d\bar q\,q-\bar q\,dq}{2s}
\end{pmatrix}.
\tag{L4}
$$
The diagonal part is the compact connection of the reductive homogeneous bundle. Its second component, the one acting on $V_n$, is
$$
A=\frac{d\bar q\,q-\bar q\,dq}{2s}.
\tag{L5}
$$
The Maurer–Cartan equation gives its curvature:
$$
\boxed{dA+A\wedge A=-\frac{d\bar q\wedge dq}{s^2}\ne0.}
\tag{L6}
$$
For example at $q=0$, evaluation on $(\partial_t,\partial_x)$ is $-2i$. On $V_n$, $n\ge1$, its action on $X^n$ is $-2inX^n$, also nonzero. Although $A$ vanishes at the origin in this frame, it does not vanish throughout a neighborhood and its curvature does not vanish even at the origin.

Consequently a global section, or the fact that the ball is contractible, does not justify replacing covariant derivatives by ordinary derivatives in this frame. A scalar change of frame adds an exact scalar one-form to the connection and does not remove this curvature. The cancellation below occurs only after projection to the particular first-order operator.

## 3. Differentiate along the group, including the compact factor

For a smooth right-K-equivariant $F$, use right differentiation
$$
(\xi_vF)(g)=\left.\frac{d}{d\varepsilon}F(g\exp(\varepsilon\xi_v))\right|_0.
$$
Factor the path through the section:
$$
\sigma(q)\exp(\varepsilon\xi_v)=\sigma(q_\varepsilon)k_\varepsilon.
$$
Its projection to the ball has derivative
$$
q'_0=v-q\bar qv=s v.
$$
Evaluating (L4) on that tangent vector, and comparing with the off-diagonal Lie algebra element $\xi_v$, shows that the second compact component satisfies
$$
(k'_0)_2=-C_v,\qquad
C_v=\tfrac12(\bar vq-\bar qv)=sA(v).
$$
Right equivariance therefore contributes the **plus** sign in
$$
\boxed{(\xi_vF)(\sigma(q))=s\,\partial_v U(q)+d\tau_n(C_v)U(q).}
\tag{L7}
$$
Indeed $F(\sigma(q_\varepsilon)k_\varepsilon)=\tau_n((k_\varepsilon)_2^{-1})U(q_\varepsilon)$, whose fibre derivative is $-d\tau_n((k'_0)_2)U$.

For explicit comparison in real coordinates:
$$
\begin{aligned}
C_1&=ix+jy+kz, & C_i&=-it+jz-ky,\\
C_j&=-iz-jt+kx, & C_k&=iy-jx-kt.
\end{aligned}
$$
The infinitesimal polynomial actions in (L1) are
$$
\begin{aligned}
d\tau_n(i)&=i(X\partial_X-Y\partial_Y),\\
d\tau_n(j)&=-Y\partial_X+X\partial_Y,\\
d\tau_n(k)&=i(Y\partial_X+X\partial_Y).
\end{aligned}
\tag{L8}
$$
These formulas make the changing-frame contribution completely explicit.

## 4. Why the projected connection is a scalar multiple of q

The cancellation identity in Liu–Zhang Lemma 3.5 becomes
$$
\sum_{v\in\{1,i,j,k\}}v\,T_n\bigl(d\tau_n(\bar vq)p\bigr)
=2(n+1)qT_np,\qquad p\in V_n.
\tag{L9}
$$
Here $d\tau_n$ has been extended to all quaternion matrices; in particular $d\tau_n(r)=nrI$ for real scalars $r$.

A direct proof avoids any assumption about a flat section. For a complex $2\times2$ matrix $M$, put
$$
R_Mp=(M_{11}X+M_{21}Y)p_X+(M_{12}X+M_{22}Y)p_Y,
\quad \mathbf T p=\binom{p_X}{p_Y},\quad E=X\partial_X+Y\partial_Y.
$$
Expansion of the four matrices $\iota(v)$ gives the differential-operator identity
$$
\sum_v\iota(v)\mathbf T\bigl(R_{\iota(\bar vq)}p\bigr)
=2\iota(q)(E+2)\mathbf T p.
\tag{L10}
$$
For example, with $q=\zeta+w j$, the first component is
$$
2\zeta(Xp_{XX}+Yp_{XY}+2p_X)
+2w(Xp_{XY}+Yp_{YY}+2p_Y);
$$
the second component has coefficients $-\bar w,\bar\zeta$ in place of $\zeta,w$. Since $\mathbf T p$ is homogeneous of degree $n-1$, $E\mathbf T p=(n-1)\mathbf T p$. This proves (L9) for every $n$, not just tested degrees.

Now $C_v=\bar vq-\langle v,q\rangle$, so (L9) and $\sum_vv\langle v,q\rangle=q$ give
$$
\boxed{\sum_v vT_n(d\tau_n(C_v)p)=(n+2)qT_np.}
\tag{L11}
$$
Thus the connection term is not zero before weighting, even after projection.

## 5. The corrected operator identity

Normalize the group operator as in P003's Killing-dual convention:
$$
\mathscr DF=\frac1{24}\sum_v vT_n(\xi_vF).
\tag{L12}
$$
This notation includes the identification of the projected target with quaternion-valued polynomials. The $1/24$ is from the Killing-dual basis, not from the flat contraction. Liu–Zhang use an orthonormal-basis formulation; a uniform nonzero normalization does not change the kernel.

Combining (L7) and (L11) proves
$$
\boxed{24(\mathscr DF)(\sigma(q))
=sD_l(T_nU)+(n+2)qT_nU.}
\tag{L13}
$$
Set $\beta=(n+2)/2$ and $U=s^\beta f$. Since $D_ls=-2q$, the product rule gives
$$
\boxed{24(\mathscr DF)(\sigma(q))
=s^{\beta+1}D_l(T_nf)=s^{(n+4)/2}D_l(T_nf).}
\tag{L14}
$$
The term $-2\beta qT_nf$ from differentiating the scalar weight cancels $(n+2)qT_nf$ exactly.

**Corrected kernel statement.** For $n\ge1$, the lift (L2) identifies smooth ball functions with the specified smooth right-K-equivariant functions, and
$$
\mathscr DF=0\text{ on }G
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
D_l\!\left(T_n\bigl(s^{-(n+2)/2}F\circ\sigma\bigr)\right)=0\text{ on }B.
\tag{L15}
$$
The nonzero factor $s^{(n+4)/2}$ in (L14) gives equivalence on the section. K-equivariance of the projected group operator extends vanishing from the section to all of $G=\sigma(B)K$. This is a smooth differential assertion; it makes no discrete-series claim at $n=1$.

For an arbitrary weight $f_\alpha=s^\alpha U$, the exact discrepancy is
$$
24(\mathscr DF)(\sigma(q))
=s^{-\alpha}\left[sD_l(T_nf_\alpha)
+(n+2+2\alpha)qT_nf_\alpha\right].
\tag{L16}
$$
P003's Theorem 3.2.4 takes $\alpha=n-2$. Its remaining coefficient is $3n-2$, nonzero throughout the stated range $n\ge2$. The alternatives $\alpha=n+2$ in (3.21) and $\alpha=(2-n)/2$ required by (3.23) leave coefficients $3n+6$ and $4$ respectively. None yields the claimed flat equation.

## 6. A counterexample within the intended equivariant domain

Take $n=2$, $v(X,Y)=X^2/2$, so $T_2v=X$. Define
$$
U(q)=s(q)^2v,\qquad
F(\sigma(q)k)=\tau_2(k_2)^{-1}U(q).
$$
This is a globally smooth right-K-equivariant function, determined by the unique section factorization. Formula (L13) gives
$$
24\mathscr DF|_\sigma
=s(-4s qX)+4q(s^2X)=0.
$$
It is also square-integrable in the induced model: $\|U\|^2s^{-4}$ is constant on the bounded ball. Thus the example is not caused by the missing equivariance hypothesis or a boundary-integrability failure.

But the printed exponent is $n-2=0$, so the paper's image is
$$
T_2(s^{n-2}U)=s^2X,\qquad
D_l(s^2X)=-4s qX\ne0.
$$
At $q=1/2$ its derivative is $-3X/2$. This disproves the claimed implication from the group kernel to Fueter regularity as printed, even under the intended extra hypotheses and the coherent replacement conventions.

The reverse implication also fails on the smooth equivariant space: take $U=v$ instead. Its printed image $X$ is regular, while $24\mathscr DF|_\sigma=4qX$. This second example is not square-integrable in the induced norm and is used only for the smooth statement. The corrected weight takes the first example to the constant regular function $X$, as expected.

## 7. Check against Liu–Zhang's actual proof

Their Proposition 3.6 differentiates the full lift (L2), rather than assuming that $U=F\circ\sigma$ has no connection terms. To see each contribution, write
$$
H_\varepsilon=1+\varepsilon\bar qv+O(\varepsilon^2),\qquad
b_\varepsilon d_\varepsilon^{-1}=q+\varepsilon s v+O(\varepsilon^2).
$$
Then the lift along the right path is
$$
F(\sigma(q)e^{\varepsilon\xi_v})
=s^\beta|H_\varepsilon|^{-2}\tau_n(H_\varepsilon^{-1})
f(q+\varepsilon s v+O(\varepsilon^2)).
$$
Differentiating yields
$$
(\xi_vF)(\sigma(q))
=s^\beta\left[s\partial_vf-d\tau_n(\bar qv)f
-2\langle v,q\rangle f\right]
=s^\beta\left[s\partial_vf+d\tau_n(\bar vq)f
-2(n+1)\langle v,q\rangle f\right].
\tag{L17}
$$
The equality uses $\bar qv+\bar vq=2\langle v,q\rangle$ and the scalar degree $n$ action. This agrees with their final derivative display on printed p. 2991. Applying the projection and (L9) cancels the last two terms, proving (L14) up to the chosen operator normalization. It also agrees with (L7) after substituting $U=s^\beta f$.

Two local slips in the printed proof should be distinguished from this valid calculation. On p. 2991 the second expression for $F(g_q\exp(tv))$ drops the factor $|q^*\operatorname{sh}(tv)+\operatorname{ch}(tv)|^{-2}$ that is required by its preceding line. Its subsequent derivative has the correct contribution from that factor. Also, the final sentence cites Lemma 3.1 for the cancellation, whereas the exact cancellation formula is Lemma 3.5. Restoring the factor and using Lemma 3.5 gives the calculation above. The source pages were visually inspected to distinguish these slips from PDF extraction artifacts.

## 8. Consequences and the remaining investigation

The proposed gauge in the initial audit is now supported both by the full source and by the connection calculation. The square between the equivariant group kernel, the weighted ball spinor, and $T_n$'s constrained quaternionic image is established at the smooth differential level. In particular the corrected ball action
$$
(\pi_\gamma f)(q)=|J|^{-2}\tau_n(J^{-1})f(\gamma^{-1}q),
\quad J=cq+d,\quad \gamma^{-1}=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{pmatrix}
$$
preserves that kernel for every $n\ge1$: it is transported left translation, the group Dirac operator commutes with left translation, and (L15) identifies the kernels. Combined with the algebraic intertwining by $T_n$ in audit B5, this proves the differential covariance of its corrected quaternionic action, beyond the earlier finite checks.

The induced norm becomes $\int_B\|f\|^2s^{n-2}dv$. Liu–Zhang's stated Hilbert range is $l>2d-1$, hence $n\ge2$ here. This comparison does not independently prove their discrete-series classification. At the end of this focused calculation, the Hilbert completion, representation parameter, and K-types remained open. The [subsequent corrected realization](corrected-realization.md) now supplies those proofs, including direct irreducibility and a closed embedding into $L^2(G)$, identifies $l=n$, and replaces the defective minimal-K-type construction by constants. This later result relies on the present differential calculation. Automorphic descent and coefficient representations remain separate open branches of R060.

The retained script checks (L4) in all four directions, (L6) on all six coordinate pairs, the base and compact derivatives, the generic differential-operator identity (L10), complete homogeneous bases in degrees 1–5, agreement of the two lift derivatives, a nonconstant spinor example, and the counterexamples. The all-degree argument is the Euler reduction above, not extrapolation from those finite bases.
